topic: Lives and service of modern Latter-day Saint prophets and apostles: historical biography
method: Fixed, editorially paraphrased source pack from official Church sources. Historical events and beliefs are represented as documented in those sources. No live retrieval or model-written fact sheets. This is a grounded multistage comparison, not a memory or retrieval benchmark.

sections.title: Russell M. Nelson
sections.body: Russell M. Nelson was born in Salt Lake City in 1924. He studied medicine at the University of Utah and completed a PhD at the University of Minnesota in 1954. He met Dantzel White while participating in a university play; they married in 1945 and had ten children. His career was in heart surgery. He operated on Spencer W. Kimball. In 1975 he was elected president of the Society for Vascular Surgery. He became Sunday School General President in 1971. He became the seventeenth President of the Church in January 2018. This section concerns historical biography, not a claim about who holds office today.

sections.title: Dallin H. Oaks
sections.body: Dallin H. Oaks was born in Provo in 1932. He graduated from Brigham Young University in accounting in 1954 and from the University of Chicago Law School in 1957. He clerked for U.S. Supreme Court Chief Justice Earl Warren in 1957–1958. He served as BYU president from 1971 to 1980, then as a Utah Supreme Court justice from 1980 to 1984. He was called to the Twelve in 1984 and served as Area President in the Philippines from 2002 to 2004. He chaired the board of the Public Broadcasting Service. He received the Canterbury Medal for religious liberty in 2013. His first wife was June Dixon; after her death he married Kristen McMain in 2000.

sections.title: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
sections.body: Dieter F. Uchtdorf was born in 1940 in Mährisch-Ostrau, Czechoslovakia, now Ostrava in the Czech Republic. He grew up in Zwickau, where his family joined the Church in 1947. He joined the German Air Force in 1959, received pilot wings in Big Spring, Texas, and fighter-pilot training in Phoenix, Arizona. He studied international management in Lausanne, Switzerland. He joined Lufthansa as a pilot in 1965 and became an airline captain in 1970. He completed his flying career on the Boeing 747. He married Harriet Reich in 1962. He was sustained to the Twelve in October 2004 and served as second counselor in the First Presidency from 2008 to January 2018.

sections.title: David A. Bednar
sections.body: David A. Bednar was born in Oakland, California, on June 15, 1952. He served a mission in southern Germany. He earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees at Brigham Young University and a doctorate in organizational behavior at Purdue University. He taught business management at Texas Tech University and the University of Arkansas. He led Ricks College, which became Brigham Young University–Idaho, from 1997 to 2004. He married Susan Kae Robinson in the Salt Lake Temple on March 20, 1975; they have three sons. He was ordained an Apostle on October 7, 2004.

sections.title: Jeffrey R. Holland
sections.body: Jeffrey R. Holland was born in St. George, Utah, on December 3, 1940. He attended Dixie High School and Dixie College. He served a mission in Great Britain from 1960 to 1962. He married Patricia Terry in the St. George Utah Temple in 1963. He earned degrees in English and religious education at BYU, then degrees in American studies at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut. He served as BYU’s ninth president from 1980 to 1989. The Anti-Defamation League gave him the Torch of Liberty Award for improving Christian-Jewish understanding. He served on the governing board of the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie, Hawaii. These are historical life events; no current office is asserted.

sections.title: Henry B. Eyring
sections.body: Henry B. Eyring was born in Princeton, New Jersey, on May 31, 1933. His nickname was Hal. He earned a physics bachelor’s degree at the University of Utah and graduate business degrees at Harvard University. He taught at Stanford University’s Graduate School of Business from 1962 to 1971. He was president of Ricks College in Rexburg, Idaho, from 1971 to 1977. He served as Church commissioner of education and as first counselor in the Presiding Bishopric before becoming an Apostle in 1995. He married Kathleen Johnson; they had four sons and two daughters. He served as a counselor to Gordon B. Hinckley in 2007–2008, then to Thomas S. Monson in 2008–2018. These are historical roles.
